incident-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT 2154321000  Elevated 5xx + tail latency observed for text-generation in eu-central. Pager: @tilly_oncall

tilly_oncall: i'm taking it. seeing p95 jump to ~2.6s and a spike in 5xx. any config changes in the last 15m?

sre_mike: metrics: fallback-rate for model rw-std in eu-central spiked ~10x at 03:12 UTC. lots of fallbacks to rw-std-q4. traces show cold KV cache misses and session 503s.

devon_ml: i rolled a routing tweak at 03:10 to prefer cheaper variants when pool capacity < 20% (policy id: policy/route-cost-threshold-2026-03). i thought it was safe but maybe transient signals tripped it.

jess_product: CS: multiple customers reporting timeouts & client retries, one high-touch customer opened a critical ticket. marking as customer-impacting.

amanda_cs: preparing status page blurb, will hold until we confirm mitigation.

tilly_oncall: i'm going to attempt a manual variant pin in eu-central to stop the oscillation. command i'm running:
```
# force rw-std -> q8 in eu-central to avoid q4 fallback while we investigate
rwctl routing set-variant --region eu-central --model rw-std --variant q8 --force --reason "INC2154321000"
```

ops-bot: accepted command, run id rwr-9912. applying to regional routing mesh.

tilly_oncall: pin applied. monitoring.

sre_mike: after the pin, we see immediate increase in cross-region reroutes: traffic spilled to us-west where reserved pools are near capacity. us-west reporting 429s and elevated latencies. :grimacing:

devon_ml: ack  the global fallback rule routes overflow to nearest region. forcing a variant bypassed the capacity-aware buckets and caused overflow. also looks like fallback doesn't respect enterprise reservations.

jess_product: so the pin stopped eu-central fallbacks but caused customer impact in us-west. what's safest now? undo the pin?

tilly_oncall: attempting unforce to let policy re-evaluate:
```
# undo forced variant in eu-central
rwctl routing unset-variant-force --region eu-central --model rw-std --reason "rollback INC2154321000"
```

ops-bot: unset complete.

sre_mike: now we're seeing a new problem: a loop where sessions flip between q8 and q4 mid-session, leading to KV-prefix mismatches and 503s. traces show node A serving q8 responses but expecting q4 KV prefixes for some RPCs.

devon_ml: yep, variant changes mid-session change KV cache namespace. quick force/unforce without draining creates sticky state. we should evict the kv prefixes and drain long-lived sessions before toggling variants.

tilly_oncall: executing mitigation:
```
infractl cache evict --pool eu-central --prefix rw-std --confirm
infractl pool drain --pool eu-central --grace 60s
```

ops-bot: cache-evict job queued (job id ce-7713). drain started.

amanda_cs: sending interim customer note: "We made a temporary routing change which caused transient degradation in some regions. Teams are mitigating and we'll follow up with a timeline and root cause." sending now. :email:

sre_mike: post-evict metrics look better. p95 and 5xx trending down, no new 429 waves in us-west.

devon_ml: preliminary root cause: 1) 'prefer-cost' policy mis-triggered on a noisy capacity signal; 2) manual force-pin bypassed regional capacity reservations and triggered global overflow; 3) rapid force/unforce led to KV prefix mismatch and session 503s.

tilly_oncall: agreed. immediate resolution steps that worked: revert the cost preference policy, evict KV prefixes in eu-central, and drain affected pools.

kevin_reliability: i'll implement a guardrail: block force-pin if it would route >10% of source region traffic to a single target region that's above 85% capacity. also adding a preflight warning in rwctl.

sre_mike: adding an alert: "variant_oscillation_detected" triggering on >3 variant flips for same session-id within 60s. owner: sre_team.

devon_ml: i'll write the postmortem and include the timeline, exact commands, tracer snippets, and recommended guardrails (prevent force-pin bypassing capacity reservations, KV-evict step in runbook, circuit breaker for oscillation).

jess_product: i'll coordinate customer follow-up and link the postmortem once ready.

amanda_cs: CS tickets updated, customers notified. one customer asked for a follow-up call, scheduled for 4pm UTC.

tilly_oncall: last check: metrics back to baseline, p95 within SLO. marking incident resolved but keeping channel pinned for postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: INCIDENT 2154321000  status: resolved. mitigation: policy revert + KV eviction + pool drain. postmortem task PM-6241 opened. pager cleared.

sre_mike: quick runbook addition: avoid consecutive force/unforce on the same pool. always drain and evict KV prefixes when changing variants in prod.

tilly_oncall: thanks all. good catch on the global fallback interactions. :thumbsup:
